beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju is thrilled seeing Kesar Paints hit a new high, sending a celebratory screenshot to Sharma ji.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji inspects the three distinct peaks and urges caution before jumping in.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju asks how one can objectively identify whether a trend is truly pausing or reversing.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Kesar Paints formed a left shoulder at ₹175, a peak head at ₹175, and is now stalling near ₹175.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The trendline connecting both correction troughs forms the vital neckline support at ₹175.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The moment price breaks below the neckline on expanding volume, the major trend reversal is confirmed.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: According to John Murphy, mastering reversal patterns requires three foundational checkpoints.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: We will study the six universal preliminary rules common to every valid reversal pattern.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Then we will unpack the complete volume sequence, return moves, and objective measurement formulas.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Reversal patterns mark a complete structural turning point, ending the prior major trend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Continuation patterns, in contrast, represent brief digestive consolidation before the trend resumes.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Traders must strictly differentiate whether the market is shifting regimes or merely taking a breath.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rule 1: A prerequisite for any reversal pattern is the existence of a prior major trend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rules 2 & 3: Breaking the major trendline warns early, while pattern height dictates price targets.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rules 4, 5 & 6: Tops form swiftly, volume must confirm, and a decisive neckline close triggers completion.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: At the left shoulder rally, aggressive bulls dominate price action on heavy volume.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: During the head's rally, price reaches a higher peak but volume visibly dries up.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: By the right shoulder, buying volume evaporates, allowing heavy selling to crack the neckline.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The neckline may be horizontal, slightly up-sloping, or down-sloping across both troughs.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: After the breakdown, price often executes a low-volume return move back toward the broken neckline.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: This return move offers traders a second chance to enter short or cleanly exit long exposure.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Measure the vertical distance from the peak of the head straight down to the neckline.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: With the head at ₹175 and the neckline at ₹175, the vertical pattern height equals ₹134.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Subtracting ₹134 from the ₹175 breakout level gives a minimum price objective of ₹175.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The Inverse Head and Shoulders forms at market bottoms, where the middle trough is deepest.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy stresses: a market can fall of its own weight, but upward breakouts REQUIRE surging volume.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If an inverse head and shoulders breakout lacks volume confirmation, suspect a false breakout.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now it's your turn to apply John Murphy's iron principles to this scenario.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think carefully about why volume expansion is non-negotiable for bullish bottom breakouts.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: High risk of a false breakout (bull trap): Murphy dictates bottom breakouts require explosive volume, as prices cannot push higher without genuine accumulation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju now realizes why anticipating patterns before neckline confirmation causes unnecessary losses.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji stresses that until the neckline closes below support, the pattern is only a thesis, not a reality.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju resolves to trade only confirmed breaks and return moves using the measured objective formula.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Today's thread: a reversal pattern demands an existing trend to reverse and a confirmed neckline breach.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Drying volume at the head and a feeble right shoulder provide early warning of the impending breakdown.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The vertical span between the head and neckline reliably projects the minimum downside target.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Crucial rule: Neckline closing violation is required to complete the pattern; Return move provides secondary entry with broken support as resistance.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Crucial rule: Target calculation: Project vertical Head-to-Neckline distance from breakout; Bottoms need volume: Inverse bottoms MUST break out on heavy volume.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The ultimate takeaway: wait for the decisive neckline close and volume confirmation before taking the trade.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Prerequisite: There must be an existing major trend to reverse
Trendline break is the first warning; pattern scale sets the objective size
Head & Shoulders Top: Head makes highest peak on diminishing volume
Right shoulder rally fails on light volume; confirms buyer exhaustion
Neckline closing violation is required to complete the pattern
Return move provides secondary entry with broken support as resistance
Target calculation: Project vertical Head-to-Neckline distance from breakout
Bottoms need volume: Inverse bottoms MUST break out on heavy volume
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
